name: Alexis Korner
hook: The bandleader whose London blues club nights were where the Rolling Stones, and half of British rock, learned to play Chicago blues.
blurb: Alexis Korner was born in Paris in 1928, to an Austrian Jewish father and a mother of Greek, Turkish and Austrian descent, and grew up partly in London. As a boy he heard a blues piano record during a German air raid and decided the blues was all he wanted to play. In 1961 he and the harmonica player Cyril Davies formed Blues Incorporated, which became a training ground. Charlie Watts, Jack Bruce and Ginger Baker played in it, and Mick Jagger, Keith Richards and Brian Jones, who went on to form the Rolling Stones, sat in. Its 'R&B from the Marquee' (1962) is one of the first British blues albums. He later presented BBC radio programmes, including 'The Rolling Stones Story' (1973), and died in 1984. In 2024 he was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame for musical influence, with Keith Richards presenting.
